title: AACP Pattern file
description: A file of known anti-patterns. INFORMATIVE — patterns are diagnoses, not obligations, and nothing here is required for conformance. A pattern's job is to answer 'why does this obligation exist?' so the obligation itself can stay short, and to act as coverage validation: a pattern that no case catches is a hole in the catalog.

domain.description: Grouping tag for this file. Presentational only — identifiers are flat across all domains.

id.description: Flat and permanent, in a namespace separate from AAC cases. Domain is metadata, not identity — the same lesson the catalog learned about archetypes.

symptom.description: What an operator observes. Written so someone can recognise it in their own system without already knowing the cause.

mechanism.description: Why it happens. The causal story that makes the obligation make sense.

caught_by.description: Obligations that would surface this pattern. MAY be empty, but only with gap_note — an empty list is a claim that the catalog does not cover this, which is a finding rather than an omission.

gap_note.description: Required when caught_by is empty. States what obligation is missing and why it has not been written yet.

signal.description: How the pattern shows in a running system's telemetry — what a monitor reads to see it before the symptom does. INFORMATIVE like the pattern: a starting rule and a starting threshold, to be tuned against the system's own baseline.

level.description: turn: decidable from one unit of work's record. conversation: needs the units of one session. window: a rate or quantile over many units, against a baseline.

reads.description: The record fields or metrics it reads. OpenTelemetry GenAI names where they exist; otherwise the AHC-0114 record group that holds it.

detect.description: The rule, in words precise enough to implement.

threshold.description: A starting threshold, where the rule has one.

severity.description: page: certain and wrong now. ticket: read this week. trend: meaningful only as a rate.
